Those speeds mean it's a great option for installing games and playing them on your Switch 2 without gameplay lag. Write speeds aren't shared, but in this class and capacity, you can usually expect up to 300 MB/s. The Samsung P9 is a microSD Express card that offers great performance and reliability for its price. The 512GB model is currently priced at its original MSRP of $99.99. You'll want the highest possible write speeds, but for a Switch 2 owner, 300 MB/s is still going to be fast enough to install new games and updates without huge waiting times. The high speeds you're seeing here will mean you won't have too big a bottleneck compared to installing directly onto the Switch 2's internal storage. That said, these speeds make the Samsung P9 Express up to four times faster than a typical UHS-I microSD card. It also ships with features to help get the most out of your card, including Host Memory Buffer (HMB) functionality to help improve data transfer speeds, along with Dynamic Thermal Guard (DTG) support to help stop the card from overheating and limiting its performance. microSD cards are small, so durability is an issue to think about, especially if you're handling it often. Samsung reckons this is a model that's well protected, even if you drop it in water, along with protection against extreme temperatures and even X-ray exposure. It has a 3-year limited warranty, and it supports Samsung's Magician software, so you can keep an eye on the card's health, as well as check if it's genuine or not (although that's not an issue here). The Switch 2 is one of the first consoles to include microSD Express support, so you can use this Samsung P9 Express card's faster storage speeds compared to older UHS-I cards. The $99.99 sale price makes this 512GB Samsung P9 a brilliant bargain to pick up ahead of the holiday season, especially if you're a current or soon-to-be Switch 2 owner. It'll give you a quick-and-easy storage upgrade ahead of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remaster launching later this week, too.

item.title: SALES: The Very Best Thai Food in New York City
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
There are several ways to describe delicious food in Thai: Aroy means delicious, while aroy mak takes it a step further to very delicious. But my favorite word is zaab (also spelled zabb or zab; แซ่บ), a term rooted in the Isan region of northeastern Thailand that conveys a bold deliciousness, often associated with the heat. In New York City, we’re spoiled for choice when it comes to food that delivers true zaab. I’ve spent my life immersed in the world of Thai food. One of the joys of growing up in a Thai restaurant family is participating in one of our favorite hobbies: scoping out other Thai restaurants to see what’s good. Most summers, my aunts would close down their restaurant in Royal Palm Beach for two weeks, and they’d road trip from South Florida up to New York City to check out casinos and taste Thai restaurants along the way—when I was lucky, I got to join them. My grandpa, for his part, used to drive to the city weekly to get products for his grocery store in Washington, DC, and through his firsthand research, old friends, and the Internet, he created detailed restaurant guides to help me find footing when I moved to the city almost five years ago. As I continue to eat my way through the city’s Thai restaurants, I feel spoiled for choice. More and more chefs are serving regional specialties of their hometowns and maintaining Thai food’s great balancing act between the spice, acid, salt, sweetness, and umami, while incorporating their own signature flair. While the city’s established Thai spots, particularly out in Elmhurst, Queens, remain beloved, plenty of the most compelling and exciting bites can be found in various parts of the city. There has never been a more exciting time to eat Thai food in NYC, and these 14 restaurants best embody its golden era. If you want an overview of the best dishes across Thailand without leaving the city, let your first stop in Queen’s Little Thai Town be Ayada. The beloved restaurant has familiar favorites like pad thai and tom yum, but let its expertise in other regional favorites be an excuse to try my dad’s favorite Yen Ta Fo, a bubblegum-pink soup with soft rice noodles and a savory tomato and bean curd sauce. 364 Grand Street, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg) Must-order dish: Any of the fiery curries on the rotating menu When the news of Ugly Baby’s closure last year hit my WhatsApp chat with my Thai friends, you would’ve thought that someone had died. In a way, it felt like we lost a family member. Ugly Baby was one of the rare spots in the city that didn’t hold back on heat like many in America do to appease Western palates and milder heat tolerances. But all was saved when the beloved restaurant announced its reopening in Williamsburg earlier this fall. It’s now a fun, lively two-floor restaurant with eclectic dishware and recipes from various Thai provinces, including brutally hot curries from Southern Thailand and Northeastern Isan cuisine. Its menu is sorted from least spicy to most spicy—written out as “the laughs” to “the ugly” (dishes toward the latter end consist of a few menu items that will make you feel like you’re breathing fire). Luckily, waiters are standing by with large jugs of water, ready to refill at the sight of sweat dripping down your forehead. 641 Hudson St, New York, NY 10014 (Meatpacking District) With an award-winning cocktail program by Suwincha "Chacha" Singsuwan and a menu from executive chef Max Wittawat, Bangkok Supper Club makes a convincing case for the arrival of upscale Thai dining. The drinks are as much of a draw as the food. I like to start my meal with a fish sauce cocktail, a savory, umami-forward drink that captures the depth of fish sauce while balancing it with sweet notes of floral pear. It’s unexpected, but feels just right, and is a lovely accompaniment to my other must-order: the pork jowl. These deep-fried pork cheeks arrive atop a fragrant, garlic-baked rice. One of the best parts about eating in Thailand is getting food from restaurants and stalls that specialize in one singular dish. As my dad says, that’s how you know it’s good. Eim Khao Mun Kai is one such place. Its one dish, khao mun gai, is the Thai version of Hainanese chicken rice, served with a spicy, fermented bean sauce. The $12 set meal includes tender steamed chicken thighs made with halal meat and gizzards, fragrant ginger rice that’s cooked with chicken droppings, and a savory broth-based soup made from the bones, with sides of cilantro and cucumber plus plenty of sauce. It’s a tight shop and cash-only. When my dad comes into town, it’s the first place we go to. Must-order dish: Northern-style curry noodles Since 1990, this institution has been serving what my friend calls “old-school auntie energy” with wooden accents, white tablecloths, and a sprawling menu. When I say sprawling, I mean it. You can flip through pages at SriPraPhai and can eat all the fried meats, papaya salads, curries, and noodle dishes your heart desires. 76-04 Woodside Ave, Queens, NY 11373 (Elmhurst) 208 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg) Zaab Zaab has locations in both Elmhurst and Williamsburg, and specializes in Northeast Isan cuisine from where owner Bryan Chunton and chef Aniwat Khotsopa hail. The restaurant’s signature dish, an herb-packed larb ped udon, features cilantro- and mint-packed ground duck, fried liver, and crispy skin; it’s served with a plethora of fresh lettuce, cabbage, extra herbs, and sticky rice. When I go with a group, though, I also make sure we order the pla neung manow, which comes steamed with a chili, garlic, and lime sauce that’s so flavorful, you’ll want to drink it like soup (luckily it’s served with little bowls so you can). 800 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg) Must-order dish: Chor muang for an appetizer; pad kea mao seafood as a main Focusing on 19th- century recipes from the royal consort court, Kaew Jao Jorm’s (named after the former King Rama V’s favorite flower) serves a regal menu in its intimate, 20-seat restaurant. The exterior is on an unassuming street in Williamsburg, but inside, it is the restaurant incarnation of Mary Poppins' bag: compact, but they manage to pack in far more than you’d expect. Though the signature dumplings, chor muang—chicken and peanut filling encased in delicate butterfly pea flower dough—are the star, don’t overlook the noodle dishes, which are slurpable, expertly sauced, and so soft as to be almost buttery. 186 Mott St, New York, NY 10012 (Nolita) If you have friends from out of town that you really want to impress and show how fun eating in New York City can be, go to Thai Diner and get an order of the Thai Disco Fries. I find that these crispy, crinkle-cut fries smothered in a peanutty massaman curry sauce are delicious enough to justify to out-of-towners how much you overspend on rent. Reservations can be hard to get, but they do take some walk-ins, so your best bet is to either arrive slightly before opening, or put your name down and wander around Nolita until your name is called. The restaurant has a tropical dive bar feel, with plenty of diner favorites reimagined like a custardy Thai tea babka, French toast, and a signature Thai Diner egg sandwich made with Isan-style sausage wrapped in a plush roti. Co-owners Ann Redding and Matt Danzer also recently opened Mommy Pai’s, a fast Thai chicken takeout spot on the same block that’s a great lunch spot without the wait. 55 Bond St, New York, NY 10012 (NoHo) 661 Driggs Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg) Must-order dish: Steamed fish with Thai herbs Specializing in seafood dishes, Fish Cheeks focuses on the bright flavors of southern coastal Thailand. Dishes are meant to be shared family-style here, and though the menu features a few poultry, pork, and beef options, your best bet is trusting the name and going straight for fish. I recommend getting a whole steamed fish for the table—your dinnermates will relish in sharing the communal centerpiece and drenching rice in its cilantro-lime broth, or the coconut crab curry, which comes with rice noodles for soaking up every last bit of the creamy sauce. Though its flagship Noho location can book out quickly, its equally delicious (and newer) spot in Williamsburg is a bit easier to secure a reservation at, for now. 40 E 20th St, New York, NY 10003 (Flatiron) If I had to describe LenLen in one word, it would be cool. This relatively new spot hit Flatiron earlier this year, bringing a fresh excitement to the Thai food scene in midtown. For me, the standout of the menu is the love-it-or-loathe-it durian crab curry. It’s earthy, fruity, and well worth the visit alone. While you’re there, order the wagyu beef boat noodles, too, which are served in a rich, dark broth that reminds me of the ones I’ve had in Ayutthaya, one of my favorite cities in Thailand (and the birthplace of boat noodles). There are whispers of a speakeasy opening downstairs in the coming months, which gives the restaurant extra potential to become a go-to dinner spot that seamlessly transitions into a night out. 417 Tompkins Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216 (Bed-Stuy) Not to be confused with LenLen, Ler Lers is a newer spot in Bed-Stuy and does classic Bangkok-style fare right. Its ambiance is stylish and warm, with a mix of rattan and earthy tones, for a setting that makes sipping on a sweet iced Thai tea feel right even on a cold rainy day. I’m pretty weary of ordering pad thai out in restaurants, just because the cuisine has so much else to offer. But a friend promised me that the pad thai topped with crispy pork belly was “awesome,” and after trying it for myself, I’ve started saying the same to friends and family. The rest of the menu has a lot of other familiar favorites like fried rice and grilled meats, and if you’re someone who enjoys a sticky tamarind sauce as much as I do, try the branzino, too. 28 7th Ave S, New York, NY 10014 (West Village) Must-order dish: panang curry beef cheek A newcomer to the West Village restaurant scene, this design-forward space has some serious pedigree with a menu curated by Bangkok-native Chattchakorn “Benz” Khajornchaisan, formerly of Eleven Madison Park. The restaurant is stylish in every sense of the word, with sage green tiles, oak accents, and warm lighting. You can’t customize spice level here, so expect to get a little red from dishes like the prik larb beef tartare that comes with crispy tripe chips and is fiery with northern larb spices. The Hommali Five Spice dry-aged duck is also a standout and comes with fragrant rice that’s cooked in duck drippings. My opinion? The best order is getting the panang curry with tender beef cheek. It’s spicy, nutty, and you’ll want to order a side (or two) of roti to soak up that sauce. The cocktail menu is also expansive—go for the signature tomato cocktail, which is vodka and rice wine-based with tomato extract, poblanos, and tamarind. 204 E 13th St, New York, NY 10003 (East Village) 25-20 43rd Ave, Long Island City, NY 11101 Must-order dish: Sukhothai-style tom yum noodle soup Thai noodle shop Soothr specializes in noodles from all across Thailand, and though the stir-fried variety is delicious, the soup noodles are the real standout. The Sukhothai-style tom yum noodle soup is a must-order, and encapsulates the best of Thai noodle soups with a deeply savory-acidic broth topped with bouncy fish cakes, meatballs, and rice noodles. Soothr has a new-ish Long Island City location that’s got a more nightlife vibe to it (and just as great noodles). 90 N 14 St, Brooklyn, NY 11249 (Williamsburg) Must-order dish: Lamb massaman curry pot pie Named after the Thai word for “mentor,” chef Ohm Suansilphong honors the many teachers in his life through Kru. Here, he draws on Thailand’s vast culinary history, reimaging regional traditions through a contemporary lens. This looks like a crispy, massaman curry pot pie sprinkled with slow-cooked, pull-apart jackfruit, and tender lamb or tamarind-chili coated calamari that’s sweet, salty, and a little spicy. Chef adds and tweaks the menu seasonally, but I suggest the first thing you eat is always the Ma Hor, a savory bite of seasoned meat atop fresh fruit. The word means galloping horse, and it has enough warmth to open your tastebuds for the rest of the meal. Pay attention to the wine list: the restaurant is just as thoughtful about its award-winning program as it is the rest of the menu. Consider this a go-to as worthy of casual weeknight dinners as it is of special occasions.

item.title: SALES: Foodie gifts to give to every epicurean in your life
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
Every year I eagerly await the arrival of Christmas – in huge part because of the impressive, creative selection of food gifts that start to land in stores late in autumn. From supermarkets to department stores, each year brings a new wave of creativity and fun, and 2026 might just be the best selection to date. To me, foodie bits make perfect presents for all ages – from stocking fillers for children to very British treats for the family friend visiting from overseas. And what’s a Christmas Day without a cheeseboard and accompaniments? To ensure you never turn up empty-handed, we’ve scoured the food gifts on offer from all of our favourite brands. From new, novelty launches to stocking fillers and show-stopping hampers, we’ve tried and tested them all to help you find the perfect gift for the foodie in your life. The best foodie Christmas gifts at-a-glance Fortnum & Mason Christmas Devils on Horseback Bacon Chutney Harrods The Sweet Taste of Christmas hamper The thought of being delivered a bag of coal would be all the more palatable if you knew it was this Selfridges offering, which comes covered in creamy milk chocolate. During our taste test, it was a firm favourite with the Traveller team. Senior commerce writer Lauren Burvill says: “They look very hard, sweet and messy, but are actually more crumbly in texture and subtle in sweetness.” Selfridges Selection Jenki Matcha Panettone A panettone is a classic gift, but comes with the risk of being somewhat typical. This matcha version, created in collaboration with matcha bar Jenki, takes a festive classic and turns it on its head. Pair with a cold glass of Bailey’s for a perfect sweet treat. Fortnum & Mason Christmas Pickled Brussel Sprouts You may imagine cold pickled sprouts to be somewhat divisive, but these tangy little festive bites won over the Traveller team. “I know they’re among the most controversial Christmas side dish, but my love of sprouts knows no bounds,” says social media manager Lucy. “Sharp, salty and tangy, they're guaranteed to shake up the tired old cheeseboard this year – nay-sayers be gone.” Acting senior audience growth manager Chloe Laws agrees: “As a Brussels sprouts and pickle fan, I had high hopes for these. They were sharp and moreish, but lacking a little crunch. For the novelty, though, they're a great cheeseboard addition.” Selfridges Selection Pigs in Blanket roasted mixed nuts An ideal snack for those in-between days, these nuts satisfy the Christmas dinner cravings. A combination of peanuts, cashews and almonds, they’re the perfect salty treat. Pop them in a stocking and cross your fingers they’ll be shared around at some point. Marks & Spencer peppermint and chocolate wafer rolls You can guarantee that these will be pulled out from the present pile and shared around at some point after dinner – and you’re going to want to be a part of it. A moreish combination of dark chocolate, thin and crispy wafer and creamy mint, we loved how easily these went down. You should actually probably buy two boxes, just in case. You don’t actually need a great cheeseboard if you have this chutney – your guests will be more than happy to scoop it onto crackers. Inspired by the festive canape of prunes wrapped in bacon, it’s full of flavour and sure to be a crowd-pleaser. Acting senior digital editor Olivia Morelli loved it: “Anything that I can add to a festive cheese board is a win for me, and this has a salty bacon edge too, which makes it super moreish.” An ideal antidote to the shrink-flation of our favourite chocolate tins in recent years, this 1.2kg tin is guaranteed to last at least past Christmas Day. Featuring lots of favourites – from salted caramel to coffee cream – you can’t go wrong if you turn up at the front door with this. These are impossibly moreish – even just thinking about them makes me want to nip over to M&S right now. My personal favourite is the blonde chocolate, but with a mix of milk and dark chocolate these are guaranteed to be crowd-pleasers. I can’t be sure you’ll get more than a handful before they’re snapped up, though. Daylesford handcrafted miniature marzipan vegetables These darling little sweet bites feel like a throwback to Christmases past, and they’re guaranteed to put a smile on your family’s faces. The combination of gorgeous packaging and colourful marzipan bites make these a gift to remember. You can’t go wrong with a great whiskey as a gift, and this Speyside single malt combines dark fruit, honey, and vanilla with layers of marzipan, cinnamon and gentle spice, for a gently festive twist on a true classic. Hear me out: this twist on mulled wine is well worth trying. Sweeter and lighter than the usual, it’s a great alternative for those who generally find mulled wine a little bit too heavy, made with English apple juice and a blend of cinnamon, clove and star anise. While the martini is having a moment, this is made for that person on your gift list who’s always impossibly chic. Made with vodka, pickle juice and olive brine, there’s a reason it’s called ‘filthy’. What could be more chic than gifting a magnum of something delicious? Whispering Angel is always a favourite, and this larger bottle will satisfy a group, making it an ideal gift for the party host. If you’re spending Christmas with someone else this year, help lighten the hosting load with this hamper that has everything you could need for a delicious Boxing Day. Stuffed with ham, a pork pie, a selection of cheeses and – my personal favourite – a bottle of mulled cider, this makes putting on a spread feel like a piece of cake. A classic Fortnum & Mason hamper is a gorgeous gift for all kinds of foodies. This Merry Christmas box features the brand’s wonderful Christmas Pudding Madeira, Christmas tea and coffee, a Christmas pudding and even Fortnum’s biscuits designed specially for pairing with champagne. What could be more indulgent? If you know someone with a sweet tooth, they’ll be blown away by this impressive hamper featuring a vast selection of chocolates, spreads and biscuits. The chocolate and biscuit collections are crowd-pleasers, while the after-dinner coffee helps with all that indulgence. Add the sweet teddy bear and you’ve gifted something special and memorable. Selfridges Selection The Buffet Selection Hamper (31 items) The host will love you if you turn up with this hamper, which is filled with everything you could need for an indulgent buffet. From crackers for cheese to chocolate, biscuits and Turkish delight, the selection is vast and varied. You also get four bottles of wine and a bottle of champagne, so absolutely everyone’s tastes will be met. Mine’s a glass of bubbly!

item.title: SALES: The best Christmas gifts to buy in London 2026
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
London is one of those cities where you can still go shopping and find something you won’t get anywhere else. It's home to a mix of heritage names and iconic fashion houses as well as a new generation of contemporary brands doing things differently. Add beautiful design, British craftsmanship and local production into the mix and you have a pretty good place to pick up a gift. From a perfectly cut shirt to a London-exclusive scent, beautiful pyjamas to little luxuries for the home, these are the gifts worth bringing back from London. The best Christmas gifts to buy in London at-a-glance Jo Malone London Rose & Oud Leather Cologne Intense - Derek Rose Arrna 20 cotton pyjama setNothing makes quite as perfect a gift as a classic pair of pyjamas. Derek Rose has been making luxury nightwear since 1926, and its cotton pyjamas have the sort of timeless appeal that makes them hard not to love. This striped set is cut from lightweight cotton with a classic button-front shirt and matching trousers. Derek Rose store are dotted around London: Notting Hill, Knightsbridge and Marylebone. - Liberty Iphis silk scarfFew things say London quite like a Liberty-print scarf. Since the department store opened its doors in 1875, its silk accessories have become a city hallmark. The Iphis is a particularly lovely iteration: a 45cm silk twill square that packs all that Liberty eccentricity into something pleasingly easy to wear. What's more? A trip to the historic store at the top of Carnaby Street is always on our list of recommendations for visitors to the capital. - Mulberry Islington suede bucket bagIn a clever nod to Mulberry's English roots, the soft Islington bucket bag is named after a particularly lovely part of north London. It's crafted in soft suede to a timeless silhouette and elevated with the understated detailing Mulberry does so well, making it an impeccable gifting choice, with or without the London connection. - Perfumer H marmalade scented candleFounded by perfumer Lyn Harris, Perfumer H creates its candle scents in London. The Marmalade candle offering a burnt citrus aroma (that might remind the nostalgic among us of our cuddly British friend, Paddington Bear). The brand's beautiful London stores are well worth seeking out while in the city. - Missoma Lucy Williams Entwine small hoop earringsA pair of hoops is always a good gift, and this design from Missoma’s long-standing collaboration with Lucy Williams is exemplary of the London-based fashion tastemaker's personal aesthetic. The mixed-metal design gives the classic hoop a sculptural twist, while the small size makes them easy to wear every day. They're designed and crafted in Missoma’s London studio. - With Nothing Underneath fine poplin shirtA classic shirt is a wardrobe staple for good reason and London-based fashion label, With Nothing Underneath, has built its entire brand around one especially good version. Inspired by mens tailoring, it's even called ‘The Classic’ and it's cut from fine-yarn organic cotton to be wonderfully lightweight. The crisp white and sky-blue options are our favourites – pick them up in the Marylebone, Belgravia and Notting Hill stores. - Jo Malone London Rose & Oud Leather Cologne IntenseWhat better excuse to bring home a Jo Malone London than as a gift for someone else? This Rose & Oud Leather Cologne Intense blends smoky leather and oud with Damask rose, patchouli and amber. It's a Harrods exclusive, so even the establishment you'll buy it form is steeped in English heritage. - Melin Tregwynt Welsh blanketA beautiful blanket is the sort of gift that works for almost anyone. This one is made from 100% lambswool at Melin Tregwynt’s mill in Pembrokeshire, using the intricate Knot Garden weave from its 1950s archive. The Mead/Ash colourway is exclusive to TOAST, making it a particularly lovely find in London. - Mason Pearson Popular hairbrushMason Pearson has been making its instantly recognisable brushes for more than 140 years, and each piece is still handcrafted in London today. The Popular is the brand’s classic piece, and it combines boar bristles with soft nylon pins to smooth and detangle with ease. It is the sort of beautifully made everyday object that you wouldn't typically buy yourself, so makes an unexpectedly good gift. - &Daughter Ava Argyle crewneckFor the person who appreciates a good jumper, &Daughter’s Ava Argyle is a top choice. Designs are made in Hawick, Scotland from super-soft Geelong lambswool and are knitted to a slightly slouchy, modern shape. Head to Liberty to shop the collection. - Aspinal of London A5 refillable journalA beautiful gift for the list-maker, note-taker or anyone who still likes putting pen to paper. British brand Aspinal of London stocks all manner of leather stationary pieces like this refillable journal is crafted from full-grain leather with a soft suede lining and gilded-edge pages. Better still, it can be personalised with initials, a name or a meaningful message, making it feel that little bit more special. - Victoria Beckham The Daily Cleansing ProtocolWhether your giftee is a beauty lover or simply someone who is often on the go, Victoria Beckham Beauty’s Travel Cleansing Duo is a winner. The set pairs its oil cleanser with a lactic acid gel cleanser in handy 50ml bottle , making it an easy way to slot the brand’s double-cleansing ritual into your hand luggage or take it on the road. It is the sort of practical little luxury that makes a lovely gift. - Drake's navy flower medallion twill tieA tie is a classic gift, but Drake’s makes the traditional feel anything but ordinary. Founded in 1977, the British brand has long been known for its colourful take on classic menswear and this silk-twill accessory is hand-rolled by dedicated tie-makers in the heart of east London. It's elegant enough to team with suiting and decorated with an ornate navy flower medallion pattern that adds interest.

item.title: SALES: Skip the high street: the best Christmas gifts are hiding in Britain's coolest hotels
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
Warm orchard cider, candles crafted from estate botanicals, blankets woven by local artisans… UK hotel boutiques have had a renaissance as of late, in step with the farm-to-fork, soil-to-skin philosophy and artisanal locality that now underpins any self respecting staycation. Their curations are perfect microcosms of the ever-evolving, and positively thriving British luxury boutique hotel scene and what ‘the good life’ now, (allegedly) entails. OUT with the big brands, the generic, global beauty classics and pashminas (why are there always so many pashminas in hotel boutiques?). IN with the hand-embroidered tablecloths stitched by village creatives, the cottagecore knits spun from the farm’s own flock, the sparkling wine whose vines weave along Britain’s meadow-to-cliff Jurassic coast, inhaling the salty air. These finely-tuned, artisanal gold mines are where to hunt for elite stocking fillers and Christmas presents, often supporting local artists and makers, usually with stories woven into them. What's more? They're nearly always wrapped and boxed with the festive magic that Blighty’s top hotels dispense like medicine year after year. This is our pick of the best festive gifts to buy from the UK's loveliest hotels. Editor's top picks of the best travel gifts for 2026 There’s no finer way to refresh one’s memory of a hobby-maxxing few days at Perthshire’s legendary glorious playground than with a bit of branded merch. Located beneath the main imposing house in the hotel’s iconic Retail Arcade, the Sporting Club dresses the outdoorsy set in sports-luxe jumpers, baseball caps and rugby shirts – all reflecting the melancholic and madly beautiful shades of the Highlands. The children’s sweaters are adorable – a sweet reminder of a stay at one of the UK’s most family-friendly luxury hotels – and while merch-minded, the women’s cream T-shirts with red statement scribbles are objectively cool, whether styled up for an evening look or worn on court. For the real Gleneagles groupies, the children’s pyjamas in various sizes would make for some seriously sweet festive scenes together. From the South African owners behind Babylonstoren, the Newt really ramped up nearby Bruton’s appeal – a sleepy Somerset village now dotted with hipster bakeries and artisanal shops flogging their wares to trendy Londoners. At the centre of this vast estate is the main honey-hued, Palladian-fronted house of architectural reverie. But it’s the bountiful kitchen gardens, the orchards, soft, sheep-grazed valleys that deliver all that festive cheer (typically in a hamper). Go for the Twelve Days of Christmas Hamper – a seasonal and festive gourmet tour of its 1,000-acres of pastures green and neighbouring farms (think local Wyvern Wing cyder, fig & plum Christmas pudding, with a pretty wreath match box for lighting it, velvety brandy butter, Somerset apple gin, and orchard-inspired Apple Panettone). The Tom's Studio x The Newt fountain pen and green writing ink with a sage candle is an elegant touch alongside the divine Somerset morsels. Originally cobbled together by Manuela Wirth as a ‘studio-to-stove’ birthday present for her husband Iwan, this coffee table tome of recipes has morphed into a who’s who of the art world… or, more specifically, who’s eating what. This is a superb present for the foodie aesthete, who’s conquered all the zeitgeisty cookbooks and is ready to tumble into the world of the original art power couple, via their recipes and those contributing – Annie Leibovitz, Ruthie Rogers and Martin Creed, no less. They’ll have got a taste for it at the Fife Arms, a reimagined Victorian coaching inn in Braemar, festooned with the couples’ art collection (Freuds, Piccassos). In fact, this Cairngorms hotel truly delivers on the boutique front, with a gift shop celebrating the very best of Scottish makers. These are all available online – tartan rugs, cashmere jumpers with tongue-in-cheek Scottish sayings, thistle-cut decanters, Albamhor soaps and creams. You’re never far from a charcuterie fiend – and this from-the-land hamper from Knepp Estates is curated with the gourmands in mind. As it happens, creatures roaming 3,500-acres of rewilded farmland in West Sussex really do taste better – and pair beautifully with English sparkling wine. Those who’ve been lucky enough to wake up at Knepp Estates in one of the treehouses, shepherd’s huts or forest cabins, before setting off on ‘safari’ with ecologists will nod emphatically. Drift through any one of rural, rustic-luxe boutique hotel group The Pigs’ kitchen gardens, and you’re bound to sniff the lingering whiff of chamomile, sage and rosemary. Crafted solely for The Pigs' bedrooms from precisely this blend of herbs, these Bespoke Bramley lotions and potions are a deep breath of the country. Nothing whisks you back to happy times like scent, and its herbaceous blend is gentle enough for lathering onto skin just before bedtime. Why not send the generous 300ml glass pump or hand and body lotion, and body wash, as well as a Bramley X Pig candle to a piggy devotee, or someone who takes their skincare provenance seriously. Transporting those in whiffing-distance to the Gladstone’s ancestral Glen Dye Highland Estate (home to descendents of the Prime Minister and dominant political figure of the Victorian era), these luxury hearth candles are crafted by Laura Thomas. Co. Finely-tuned to mimic the smells and sensations of soaking in one of Glen Dye’s outdoor forest baths, the scent blends fir and pine, with orange, cinnamon, clove and palmarosa essential oils. For those whose heart is in the Highlands, why not combine this with estate honey, jams and jellies for a thoughtful, transportative Christmas present. Sister Estate, Gladstone Hellen in Wales has also curated a locally-led trove of presents – fair isle jumpers, willow basket bags, 6 bottles of Hawarden estate apple sauce – all supporting local artisans or showcasing bounty from this family’s three regenerated estates (where you can now stay and eat like a Gaelic King). The village pub, a pillar of British society, the cornerstone of the community and, increasingly, beneficiary of the rustic glow up and menu overhaul. Great Durnford’s 19th-century inn in Wiltshire fits the brief, lost in the coils of the River Avon and rolling Woodford Valley meadows. Along with the cosy, beamed-and-earthy rooms and the restaurant, where Head Chef Jordan Taylor whips top-flight countryside bounty into swishy modern plates, there’s a terrific farm shop flogging your usual organic suspects – Durnford jams, chutneys, fresh kitchen garden veg, Durnford Estates game, and body creams and oils concocted on site from estate botanicals. Durnford’s Nourish & Restore Trio is the ultimate soil-to-skin armour for winter with its lip balm, face balm and signature body oil, all packed with vitamin E, rose and carrot extracts and lemon and mint essential oils. Lime Wood’s Herb House Spa is underpinned by the remedial powers of nature, making the most of Lime Wood’s bucolic New Forest surroundings, along with a holistic approach to wellness (both mind and body). It’s a natural fit then for the Hampshire hotel to partner with Dorset-based Sae Seaweed who hand-harvests the marine miracle plant from the coast at Studland under license from the Crown Estate. Guests will feel the healing, detoxifying powers of Sae Seaweed (rich in marine minerals and vitamin E) through bespoke treatments and bathing rituals at Herb House, or now at home, with their frankincense, lavender, geranium and grapefruit lotions and oils – available at the spa shop or online. Acres and acres of bucolic, sheep-flecked countryside, woodland and parkland, Cowdray is one of England’s greenest, prettiest estates. From its infamous ruins to its design-den treehouses, it's a superb weekending spot (under two-hours from London), with scenic walks in all directions through the rolling Sussex Downs. With all these acres comes a first-class, larder, one you can stick your snout into at the estate’s Farm Shop, or one of Cowdray’s Wellbeing hampers. Brimming with nourishing, local treats such as Cowdray Kefir (from the estate’s herd by local maker, Susana & Daughters), Kentish Cherry Juice, Sauerkraut from The Sauerkraut Company and Holos Kombucha (both based in West Sussex). For extra Christmas spirit points, many of the hamper goodies are from UK-based B Corp companies, such as Mission Tea, Swole Panda Socks and Bramley botanicals. Hear Hear! Claridges’ Christmas pudding – a century-old, secret recipe whispered down through the hotel chefs – is almost as legendary as the Deco grande dame’s afternoon tea. It’s the ultimate token of gourmand goodwill - a perfectly British Christmas pudding (beautifully presented in a porcelain bowl and boxed and ribboned with that fancy, five-star hotel panache and iconic, Claridge's turquoise. And if you happen to be in the neighbourhood, why not pop in for a few festive cocktails or high tea? 'Tis the season. From the Durslade Farm Estate, where Hauser & Wirth’s Somerset gallery is located, and the legendary Farm Shop (you’ll find its little sister in Mayfair) this Winter Spiced Negroni is the small-but-mighty stocking filler – a souvenir from a jolly West, or a suggestion for 2027. Distilled with festive aromatics – cloves, nutmeg and star anise – the spiced negroni has a reassuring kick and is best nursed by a crackling fire to Michael Bublé. The Torridon’s first original gin was a labour of love, or lovage, Scots Lovage… along with other foraged botanicals: bilberries, rowanberries, and kelp seaweed blended with pure Scottish loch water. Not only is the gin crisp, clean and deliciously dry, but a majestic stag poses on its bottle, the very beast roaming old glen-and-loch Caledonia engulfing this turreted Highland hotel. Teffont House sits in the village of Teffont Evias in Wiltshire’s Nadder Valley – a rural idyll of chalk streams, water meadows and thatched cottages framed by foxgloves and delphinium. Londoners and locals retreat here to curl up by the fire with a Bloody Mary and no bloody plans… a sauna and cold plunge, perhaps, badminton or croquet in the walled garden, possibly, and duck fat chips and jaffles on the terrace. Definitely. Just beside the sauna sits a small treatment room, where therapists lather botanically-pure Bramley products onto weary backs – all of which can be wrapped up and sent as a delicious-smelling gift. Hand illustrated by journalist Suzannah Taylor, the boxes, such as the wellness tent, are particularly pretty and brimming with self-care treats: pillow spray, bubble bath, body lotion, calm balm, shower oil and a travel candle. Anyone who’s stayed as this Belgravia-based, unapologetic old timer will be familiar with its traditional rhythms, its royal stamp of approval, and its tangible sense of fun (think Shetland ponies and riotous summer parties). The Goring Cocktail Bar may resemble a swanky Gents’ Club, with its velvet banquettes, rows of amber whiskies and a roaring fire, but you’ll find a smart set propped up at the deco bar with squiffy intentions. The G&T’s and martini’s never fail to be of service, and The Gin of The Goring (infused with natural botanicals and apricots grown in its own gardens) is a thoughtful gift to transport drinking partners straight back to that stool, on that night, at that Belgravia hotel. Envisage a shrunk-in-the-wash Gothic castle… shrunk without losing any of the tapestry, velvet, panelling pomp. The Witchery by the Castle is Edinburgh’s theatrical, 17th century stay, with mahogany four poster beds, candle-lit evenings and haggis mornings. Unsurprisingly, it's rather good at tartan, particularly in its gift shop (a paean to Scottish craftsmanship) where tartan queen, Araminta Campbell’s designs for the Witchery fit snugly onto hot water bottles – the ultimate companion for those brutal Scottish winters. A monopoly board from the Ritz seems a fitting present for hard-to-buy-for. Players can immerse themselves in the glitzy Mayfair and St James world of London’s legendary grande dame while whooping their opponents. The hotel itself is the ultimate embodiment of a traditional London Christmas – well worth a festive afternoon tea to break up a long day of Christmas shopping or, indeed, an indulgent stay in one of the hotel’s ornate, velvet-and-gilt-mirror suites. Fanning out across Southrop, a pretty Cotswolds village of honey-stone houses, barns and cottages, Thyme is all soft, rural idyll. At its helm is the Hibbert family, whose passion and profound reverence for the beauty and rural bounty surrounding the Estate conjures up beautiful, meaningful gifts. The spa and rooms are stocked with Bertioli products – scents and patterns reflect the region’s precious meadowlands. Botanical essential oils with notes of water mint and wild grasses are immediately shoulder-lowering, and the eco-credentials, inspiring (eliminating throwaway plastic and reducing their carbon footprint). Treat someone in need of a few slow mornings to the Breathing balm, double wick scented Bertioli candle or even a luxurious Bertioli silk bathrobe. One of London’s smoothest, most elegant drinking holes, Scarfes Bar at Rosewood London is a dark-wooded, jazz-fuelled winter warmer with terrific cocktails. Those who’ve quaffed negronis and ‘on yer bikes’ here will be acutely aware of celebrity illustrator Gerald Scarfe’s caricatures framed throughout and peppered across the cocktail menus. They’re also scribbled across the playing cards that accompany various gift boxes of standout cocktails and bar sets. Why not bring Holborn’s suavest drinking den (and a taste of Japan) home for someone in need of a fancy tipple this Christmas with this cool collaboration (including the limited edition KINKÕ bottled cocktail, playing cards of Scarfe’s most iconic sketches and two handmade glass whisky tumblers? Kit Kemp’s signature playful, kooky and colourful interiors dress all the Firmdale Collection hotels, from Soho’s Hamyard and Charlotte Street Hotel to New York’s Warren Street Hotel in Tribeca. There’s the instant pang of familiarity when you walk into one of the group’s vibrant, bold patterned, arty numbers, and for anyone with memories here or, just a love of Kit Kemp’s design, her Blue Tall Trees ceramic candle is a stellar Christmas present. And it smells as delicious as it looks: pink pepper, warm cedarwood and soothing purple patchouli. Whether you’ve curled up at the Marylebone after a leisurely mooch around its independents, dropped bags at the Bloomsbury in London’s literary heartland or have hunkered down in the Kensington for afternoon tea and no plans, you’ll have caught the subtle notes of bergamot lingering in the air of all Doyle Collection cousins. Let it linger on beyond a stay, as a gift to a friend or loved one sharing special memories at a Doyle number… This reassuringly chic and heavy candle, features a subtle metallic glass that would give even the dullest of bathrooms or bedrooms an instant glow up. Hand-poured in Ireland by master perfumers, Cloon Keen, using vegetable and mineral wax with Italian cotton wicks, this elite candle is almost too good (and too heavy) for stockings – elves have been known to redirect it beneath the Christmas tree.

item.title: SALES: Christmas gifts for gap-year travellers: what to buy
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
Embarking on a gap year is a rite of passage, but packing for months on the road isn’t easy. The key is to ensure that everything you're bringing earns its place in a backpack – useful picks that are durable enough to withstand being hauled about from plane to train to hostel, have a proper space-saving design, and add a touch of something special to very no-frills travel. Our curated edit takes the guesswork out of gifting for intrepid young travellers, regardless of whether they’re hopping on sleeper trains across Southeast Asia or road tripping along Australia’s coast. The below items have been tried, tested and loved by our jetsetting editors over years, keeping us safe and comfortable on the move – so we're sure they'll do your loved one proud, too. From cosy loungewear sets for long-haul flights to a beloved pair of comfortable trainers and a capacious waterproof backpack, these practical, editor-approved gifts ensure young travellers will hit the road fully prepared for the adventure of a lifetime. Paire Full Brief Lipstick Underwear™ (Pack of three) - Intrepid Travel gift voucherNow this is how to do your gap year properly. Intrepid Travel has some of the most incredible group tours you can take – think crossing the Antarctic circle, island hopping across the Galapagos and trekking up Machu Picchu – so this gift card allows the most adventurous soul you know to live their best life however they choose, valid for up to five years, so they’ve time to choose wisely. Name a better way to spend your time out. See our full guide to the best group adventure holidays. - Stubble & Co Travel BackpackAnyone who thought backpacks are solely for those who pack light, think again. This editor-favourite rucksack by Stubble & Co has an impressive 42L capacity and can easily step in as an in-flight carry-on for long-haul gap year flights. It’s sized specifically for airline cabins, with helpful compression straps to squeeze everything in, so it’s perfect for hostel-hopping and itineraries with various stops. The external shell is waterproof and it comes with a reflective rain cover, clamshell opening, hidden valuables pocket, and padded laptop sleeve. All in all, it’s an ultra-durable best friend for a few months spent on the road. See all of our backpack recommendations in our travel backpack guide. Editor review: “I’ve loved a few backpacks over the years, but none has ever quite become ‘the one’: the Gandys bag that’s a touch narrow for laptops; the Patagonia duffel/backpack hybrid that’s great for the beach but too big to keep things neat on a weekender; the admittedly fake Belstaff rucksack with fraying straps etc. The Adventure Bag from British B Corp-certified bag specialists Stubble & Co has none of these drawbacks. It’s big enough (42 litres) to cover a long weekend, but not too big for daily use, and packed with features: the secret pocket, the padded laptop compartment, the clamshell design that means it can effectively open out like a suitcase, with a special pocket for my frequently dirty trainers (big tick). Using it on a recent trip to Comporta, as well as on my regular overnighters in London, it never felt over-engineered or fussy, and I loved the top compartments for books and gadgets. The real joy is its versatility. It nicely straddles city and outdoor style, and if you use the waist straps and take the extra waterproof cover (it’s already waterproof) it feels like it could handle a proper expedition. Made from recycled plastic, with strong YKK zips, it feels robust and well-made. I think I’ve found the one,” Toby Skinner, former features director - ByMatter Liquid Iron wrinkle release fabric sprayLet’s face it – we can’t imagine any gap year traveller is going to spend too much time diligently ironing their clothes in a hostel laundry room. Gift them this spray instead. It uses a heat-free formula to relax fibres on contact, meaning you can leave the steamer at home. At 90ml, it’s carry-on compliant, slipping easily into a backpack or washbag. The fragrance is lovely too, smelling of sandalwood, palo santo, and pink pepper, and so it doubles as a fabric refresher to keep worn clothes smelling clean between launderette stops on long trips. See our full review of this spray in our Liquid Iron review. Editor review: “I tried this spray on a floaty blue summer dress on a recent trip to Portugal. The spray worked impressively, restoring its shape to a decent degree in under two minutes. It did leave a little damp patch, but this dried down quickly. It is a little expensive at £24 for 90ml and, of course, don’t expect it to do as good a job as your regular iron. Nonetheless, if you’re looking for a completely fuss-free and quick way to help drop stubborn creases in your clothes, this does the job. It’s earned a permanent spot in my travel washbag going forward.” Sarah Bannerman, commerce editor - Cabeau The Neck's Evolution, TNE S3 travel pillowA basic travel pillow won’t cut it on overnight sleeper buses and long-haul economy flights, especially if you’re doing a lot of travelling in a short space of time. So treat your jetsetter to our editor’s favourite – and by far our bestselling – instead. This B-Corp-certified memory foam pillow offers firm support, moulding to your shape with an adjustable toggle clasp and chin strap to stop head-bobbing – you can even strap it to the seat headrests so you can lean fully against it for some actual decent rest. A handy side pocket stores earplugs for noisy hostel dorms, making it an essential upgrade for improving comfort on the road. See all of our recommendations in our full guide to the best travel pillows. Editor review: “I tested this pillow when I flew to Mexico City. The foam in it is extremely comfortable, but what I love most is that the back of the pillow is flat, so you can sit right up against your seat, unlike the typical travel pillow styles, which tend to be round and tilt your neck down slightly. The straps are a great idea, but if you're short it might not be possible to secure to the headrest, so keep that in mind. It also comes in a sleek cylindrical bag that, when clipped onto your carry-on luggage, you’d never even know there was a travel pillow inside." Sarah Allard, digital director - Béis sport slingI love this bag, which is suited for far more than just navigating airport terminals, packing in a hidden water bottle holder, phone sleeve, and multiple card slots into a svelte streamlined shape. It’s Ideal for day trips, city breaks and coastal hikes alike – I’ve even used it horse riding on several occasions. It keeps your daily essentials secure and close to your chest without requiring a bulky daypack, and it comes in six versatile colourways that should match any other Beis pieces you own. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best sling bags. Editor review: “A niche thing I noticed but one I appreciated – I wore this sling bag on a snowshoe expedition while wearing a huge thick puffer coat, and the strap allowed me to let it out long enough to cover my very bulky jacket without discomfort. I loved how the secret water bottle sleeve could pop out too – it was great to be able to head out without a bulky backpack just so I could stay hydrated on-the-move.” Charley Ward, commerce writer - Lifesystems Pocket First Aid KitLifesystems developed the UK’s first travel-specific first aid kit, becoming a staple for hikers and backpackers. This Pocket Kit is lightweight and housed in a durable, rip-resistant case – ideal for throwing into a daypack in case of scooter accidents, or scrapes and bruises from jungly treks and hikes. Simply top it up with local painkillers or blister plasters for essential peace of mind when heading off the beaten track. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best first aid kits for travellers. - Sony 1000X series WF-1000XM6 wireless noise cancelling headphonesBlock out noisy hostel dorms, roaring airplane engines, and chaotic night buses with these Sony earbuds, which hit a gold standard for noise-cancelling technology. Four microphone sensors intelligently adapt to your surroundings, while four tip sizes mean you can guarantee a comfortable, secure fit on the move. They have eight hours of battery life before needing to be charged – just pop them back into the case for more juice. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best noise-cancelling headphones. Editor review: I travel a lot for work, so finding a pair comfortable enough for long haul flights, while able to drown out all of the hubbub that comes with airports and planes, was key. Happily, this pair delivers on both counts. They come with four sizes of earbud tips that can be easily attached, so they feel super secure and comfortable for long periods of time. The sound and noise cancelling is perhaps the best I’ve experienced – they contain four microphones that cleverly track the noise around you (weather, traffic, talking) and then adapt accordingly. I found it really easy to connect them with my laptop and phone, and the battery life lasts for an impressive eight hours. The fact that the curved, pebble-coloured case looks great perched on my desk is a bonus. Sarah Allard, digital director - Airbnb gift cardThis one’s a real goodie; one that will be sorely appreciated after a long stint in a bunk bed or tent. An Airbnb gift card is a flexible gift that they can cash in when hostel dorms get overwhelming and they need a reset, a pool, or a cosy base between long travel stints. - Ever Vessel Multi water bottleNow there are thousands of bottles out there each promising to fulfil your every requirement – but this one might be the best so far for frequent travellers (the Stanley is far too cumbersome to pack in your carry-on or underseat cabin bag). It also has a number of features other bottles in this list can’t claim, including a tea strainer and optional shake whisk, so it’s as good for your hand luggage as it is for your morning tea and post-gym protein shake. The ultimate do-it-all companion when you’re looking to pack light. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best reusable water bottles. Editor review: “At 500ml, the Multi toes the line between being large enough to see me through a half-day’s activities and small enough to slip comfortably into my backpack’s bottle holder. It’s double-wall insulated so is suitable for hot and cold drinks and, after a good test, I’m really impressed with its insulating qualities. Cold drinks have stayed that way all day and, while I’ve not tested the full 12-hour staying power for hot drinks, I can confirm that my pre-work tea consistently remains hot for the duration of my 50-minute commute.” Charley Ward, commerce writer - Hydrapak Seeker crushable bottlePerfect for camping trips, multi-day hikes, and off-grid adventures, this bottle holds an impressive three litres while weighing a mere 92 grams. It’s made from a durable TPU that easily handles hot and cold liquids, straps to a rucksack via a D-ring and squashes down completely flat when empty, saving precious backpack space for your clothes and shoes. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best collapsible water bottles. - Antler packing cubes in monogramSay goodbye to having to pull everything out of your bag just so you can reach your clean socks at the bottom. These Antler packing cubes keep clothes compressed and orderly inside cramped backpacks or duffels. They’re an editor-favourite thanks to their durable build quality and breathable mesh lids, which makes rooting through your pack in a dark hostel room quick and hassle-free. We love the smart monogram design, too. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best packing cubes. Editor review: “From extensive long-haul trips to the Maldives and Australia to city breaks in Paris where I've had carry-on luggage only, I’ve used these on so many trips. Antler stands out as one of the premier luggage brands in the UK; the build quality is stellar and the mesh lids make it so easy to spot what is stored inside.” Lauren Burvill, senior commerce writer - Stackers hanging wash bagThis compact hanging washbag is one of my favourite finds of 2026. It has multiple zipped pockets, and a handy top hook that makes it a lifesaver for keeping toiletries off wet communal shower floors. I also love the removable clear pouch, which makes life far easier at airport security. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best travel washbags. - Burga vintage magnetic power bankNobody likes the idea of a loved one away on the road with a dead phone. Any battery anxiety on the road now becomes a thing of the past with this magnetic MagSafe power bank. It offers an impressive 15,000 mAh capacity, meaning it can recharge a phone three to four times before needing a recharge, helping you stay connected on long-distance bus rides or off-grid camping trips alike. As a bonus, who knew a power bank could look this cute? See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best portable chargers. Editor review: It’s weird to rave about a phone charger, but I genuinely love this – I have the largest 15,000 mAh and, while it is a little heavy, low-battery anxiety is now a thing of the past for me. I solo travel pretty often so this is a really big deal – this charger will comfortably top up my phone on three to four occasions – and it does so pleasingly speedily, too. I’ve also got the matching phone case and ring stand, which have generated plenty of compliments. Style plus substance? It’s a winner for me. Charley Ward, commerce writer - Papier All Abroad travel journalLess practical, but a lovely keepsake idea – a travel diary helps your gap year traveller commemorate every milestone, new friend, and memory made while on the road. See all of our recommendations in our guide to the best travel journals. - Classic Bikini Lipstick underwear (Pack of three)Rolling down to the size of a lipstick tube, Paire’s briefs are a gamechanger for backpackers or anyone who’s off packing light. They’re made from an antibacterial, odour-resistant regenerated silk blend, so they dry swiftly after a quick wash in the sink – they’re a perfect accompaniment to hot climates and long transit days. Editor review: “I wore these on a mega schlep from the UK to Indonesia, which required three long flights in quick succession. There was no VPL under my leggings or my t-shirt, and the generous stretch made both pieces more than comfortable enough for a long-haul flight. Travel aside, I wouldn’t hesitate to wear the knickers for a gym class or a full-day hike.” Charley Ward, commerce writer - Tessan universal travel adapterAn all-in-one essential for country-hopping gap year itineraries. This adapter has multiple USB ports, allowing travellers to charge phones, cameras, and power banks simultaneously from a single wall outlet anywhere in the world with just one plug – phew. See our full guide to the best travel accessories. - Amazon KindleNobody wants to carry multiple paperbacks when space in your luggage is at a premium, so a Kindle is a fantastic way to brin gall the books you could ever need while adding mere grams to your luggage allowance. This new iteration has a 25 per cent brighter light than previous models, and one charge will last you weeks – potentially your whole trip. You’ll want to slip one in your bag for night buses, lounging sessions, and long airport layovers. See our full guide to the best e-readers. - Alo Yoga Alosoft cropped technical topIf you love the slouchy style of the Adanola tracksuits but you want something less sporty, more elegant, Alo Yoga is the best loungewear brand for you. There’s a reason the style set is regularly spotted kitted out in this US activewear brand. They’re known for creating quality, fashion-forward pieces that take the likes of Gigi Hadid, Taylor Swift, Kendall Jenner and Hailey Bieber seamlessly from pilates class to brunch. Although some of these sets are loose-fitting, with comfort and freedom of movement at the forefront of the designs, others are more body-sculpting, if you prefer a form-hugging look. - Sisterly Tribe Softsculpt leggingsThese soft, sculpting leggings have been proven over and over while our editors have logged serious air miles. The stretchy matte material is both bobble-resistant and flattering, and we’ve worn them everywhere from long-haul flights to mountain hikes and morning yoga sessions on the beach. For a comfy yet flattering go-to outfit, these are excellent. Editor review: “Of all the activewear in my collection, these Sisterly Tribe yoga pants have logged the most air miles with me. They have accompanied me to a wellness retreat in Saint-Tropez, reformer sessions in Marbella, and rugged backcountry trails across Wyoming. Despite dozens of machine washes, the material has never bobbled or lost shape (unlike other premium alternatives). The deep charcoal tone flatters every skin tone and pairs effortlessly with neutrals, pinks, and whites. They transition smoothly from airport lounges to post-workout coffees without looking scruffy. On gym days, I am genuinely disappointed if they are still in the laundry basket. I look forward to wearing them every single time and plan to pick up the flared version next so I am never without a pair.” Charley Ward, commerce writer - New Balance 9060 trainerUS associate editor Charlie Hobbs waxed poetic last year about his long-standing love for New Balance dad shoes. His claim: They are the ultimate travel shoe. Among his favourites are the popular 9060 sneakers. “They are the only trainers I pack," says Hobbs. “My conservatism is rewarded. I am obsessed with these. They are so comfortable, the Platonic ideal of the walking shoe.” They shine for both style and comfort and work well year-round. “The shoes don't merely survive such 30,000 step days – they improve, becoming softer, easier to wear, and never staining with the dust of the Tiergarten,” says Hobbs. See our full guide to the best trainers for travel.

item.title: SALES: What Condé Nast Traveller editors actually want for Christmas
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
What do the editors of Condé Nast Traveller actually want to find under the tree? After a busy year checking into hotels worldwide, logging serious long-haul flight hours, and discovering plenty of special treasures along the way, our team has compiled their ultimate holiday wishlists. From tried-and-tested carry-on upgrades and smart knitwear to Korean beauty cult favourites and games tailored for long flights, we’ve rounded up all of the pieces topping our lists this season. So whether you’re searching for inspiration for your loved ones – or looking to drop a subtle hint of your own, let our editors guide your festive gifting this season. Every year, my family asks me what I want for Christmas; every year, I’m left wracking my brains at the last minute for suitable suggestions. I draw a blank, despite the fact I’ve spent the past 11 months with a mental list full of things I need (ok want). But not this year. Condé Nast Traveller’s very first Christmas gift guide was the perfect excuse to get my act together and commit to a list of all the things my heart most desires well in advance. Chill time at home between trips is just as important as the adventures themselves, so I’ve been gradually updating our interiors with accessories that make staying in feel as special as possible. I try to gather inspiration from the beautiful hotels I’m so lucky to visit, and can’t resist pieces that manage to cleverly combine thoughtful design with a cosy, lived-in feel. Soho Home’s Rio portable lamp, with its sculptural glass shade and dark marble base, is top of my wish list. Confession: I love a list. Any time of year, any theme. It’s about the only thing that I still commit to using a physical notebook and a pen to write, so there’s something wonderfully nostalgic about the whole experience, especially come Christmastime. By November, lists aren’t just about Things To Do but where to go and what to buy, and that feels exciting to me. Is there anything better than knowing your present for someone is spot on? For 2026, my winter calendar involves trips to two new bucket list spots as well as ample time in the English countryside for uninterrupted family time. My personal picks reflect my plans, which include a stay at one of Austria’s whizziest family-friendly hotels and a visit to Finnish Lapland on the chase for the Northern Lights, as well as lots of nothing at all. Nothing pairs better with a passport than a beautifully packed washbag, and this season, these top my list. Dior's Forever Glow Luminizer, is a gorgeous vintage-style compact with peachy-gold finely milled powder. It’s beautiful on cheekbones, lids and collarbones, catching the light perfectly. Perfume is always at the top of my travel agenda. And Chanel's new Paris–St. Moritz bottles Gabrielle's Alpine escapes into a pear, rose and musk laced fragrance that smells like a fresh winter holiday you can wear. Can't get away? Jo Malone's Vanilla Scotch candle conjures a Highlands fireside from the sofa, or makes the chicest host gift for a country-house weekend. Frequent flyers will love the Sephora Favorites Advent Calendar, whose minis are washbag gold, and Estée Lauder's Blockbuster is the ultimate at-home beauty kit with eight full sizes arriving in a very useful makeup bag. And for the gadget lover? Dyson's camera-guided CameraJet brushes and flosses in one go, so your hotel bathroom routine just got smarter and easier. I’ve had a very work-hard-play-hard kind of year, having jumped on a plane at least once a month to check in somewhere exciting for Traveller – and still with a couple more trips to go. My Christmas wishlist reflects this energy, incorporating some of my favourite finds from the year’s travels, along with other pieces that make jet-setting that little bit easier. I’ve become a complete Korean skincare convert after a trip to Seoul in May, and fell in love with Le Labo after my suite’s bathroom at Fairmont Hanoi was stocked exclusively with its toiletries in Vietnam. Anyone who’s a regular long-haul traveller will be happy to learn that the most superior NYT game, Connections, has just been released as a physical puzzle book – I’m not ashamed to admit that I’ve completed over 1,000 of these on the app – so that should keep me happy for a few hours on my next plane ride. I’ve a trip to NYC next month and every city breaker needs a good pair of comfy trainers for the inevitable 30,000-step days; New Balance’s iconic 9060s are the obvious choice. Finally, these sleek wrist and ankle weights are super carry-on friendly, helping to maximise results from morning runs and Pilates sessions, whether at home or away. I’m a Libra and Librans like nice things; leather things, sparkly things and nice smelling things. Function has never really been my forte. Travelling in this job, I’ve also been privy to many nice things this year – a private yacht in the South of France, a private villa in Thailand, a mountain top hotel in Switzerland. Drawing on this nice things research, I’ve come up with a magpie’s list of frivolous nice things for my Christmas wishlist. Thank you Santa. I'm an emotionally-driven shopper and my friends and family know it: in the same vein, the best gifts I've ever received are the ones money can't buy. That said, each item on my list below feels like a gateway to some of the things that bring me the most joy. In chronological order, we have martinis with loved ones, laughter and awe, storytelling, skiing through powder-soft snow, music in the old school sense, and – waking up in the morning! And the physical things necessary to remember it all or do it all over again next year. Every item in this gifts for travellers guide has earned its place through rigorous, real-world testing by our team of seasoned editors. As frequent flyers who spend much of the year on the move, we don’t just recommend products based on how they look on a shelf – we take them on long-haul flights, pack them into overhead lockers, drag them along cobblestones and put them through their paces on everything from quick weekenders to long-haul assignments. From checking the smooth roll of a carry-on’s wheels to ensuring a sleep mask stays comfortable for eight hours at 30,000 feet, we only include the travel gear, tech and accessories that we genuinely rely on ourselves and love enough to give to our own friends and family. As a travel and commerce writer for Condé Nast Traveller for the last three years, plus a further four-year stint writing shopping guides for Good Housekeeping, I have tested hundreds of products – so I know how to find the best of the best. I spend a large portion of my time living out of a suitcase, trialling gear on the move – I tend to take at least one flight a month. It means my recommendations are grounded in hands-on experience, with most products tried out over a considerable length of time.

item.title: SALES: Sommelier-Approved Thanksgiving Wines
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit
The challenge of picking wine for Thanksgiving is multifaceted. Your selections must be lively enough to enjoy as guests work their way through charcuterie, balanced enough to play well with turkey, and versatile enough to rub shoulders with dessert. It’s a tall order for anyone tasked with bringing the bottles to their holiday meal. To help, five beloved wine-heads from across the country weighed in on the bottles that everyone around your holiday table will adore. Here are the crowd-pleasing offerings sure to liven up your Thanksgiving. Bérêche & Fils Brut Champagne Réserve NV For Adam Robins, beverage director at State Bird Provisions and The Progress in San Francisco, there’s no better way to start a festive meal than with Champagne. Bérêche & Fils delivers classic brioche notes tempered with fruit like Bosc and Asian pears, brought together with a snap of acidity to prime the palate for the feast ahead Les Cigales dans la Fourmilière Escarpolette Blanc 2024 Los Angeles’s Lasita is beloved for its natural wine selections and its menu of kicky Filipino favorites. Co-owners Chase and Steff Valencia adore this Languedoc orange wine, which offers notes of bold fruit—peach and apricot—and a bright acidity that can cut through even the butteriest of mashed potatoes. Peter Lauer Riesling Schonfels Kabinett No. 111 “More people should be drinking Riesling,” says Matt Turner of Lei, one of Bon Appétit’s Best New Restaurants of 2026. He points to this German stunner with direct minerality and notes of stone fruit, which sips just as well alongside a cheesy cauliflower gratinée as a garlic-studded beef tenderloin. At the James Beard–nominated Wild Child in Lafayette, Louisiana, natural wine rules supreme. Ian LaCour, who helps curate the bottle list, gravitates toward this muscular red. Thanks to a silky body and dusky notes of stewed red fruit, it plays well with the “heartier proteins on the Thanksgiving table.” You’d be forgiven for being unfamiliar with macvin, a niche style of fortified wine made in France’s Jura region. But the oaky fresh apple and cider notes in this punchy bottling—akin to a less-oxidized, sweeter oloroso sherry—make for a divine digestif. “It fares well with every dessert,” says Nick Arone of Detroit’s Bar Chenin.
